resources.string: Please read the following terms carefully before using this app

AI Pocket Chat is an AI virtual companion chat application. By its nature, it is a client-side tool. All characters are powered by artificial intelligence and are not real people. AI-generated responses are based on language model algorithms and may contain inaccurate, incomplete, or inappropriate content.

Important: This application does not generate AI content itself. All AI responses are generated by third-party AI service providers (such as OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, Google Gemini, etc.) that you select and configure. The developer is not a generative AI service provider and does not participate in the training, operation, content moderation, or any form of content generation by third-party models.

The app is provided as is, and the developer makes no warranty as to its availability or continuity.

You must be at least 18 years old to use this application. Minors are prohibited from using this application. If a minor accesses this application through a guardian\'s device, the guardian is responsible for supervising device use and bears full responsibility for any related consequences.

When using this app, you agree not to:
• Send illegal, pornographic, violent, or harassing content
• Use AI to generate harmful, fraudulent, or misleading information
• Attempt to bypass content safety measures

About content you create: All content you create within this application (including but not limited to character cards, conversation records, social posts, diary entries, stickers, etc.) is created and edited entirely by yourself. The developer does not pre-review, moderate, monitor, or endorse any user-created content. You bear full legal responsibility for all content you create, save, or share. The developer reserves the right to cooperate with investigations as required by law.

You are responsible for ensuring that your use complies with the laws and regulations applicable in your location.

AI character responses do not constitute any professional advice, including but not limited to medical, mental health, legal, or financial advice. AI-generated content may be factually incorrect, may contain biases, and may be fabricated, and does not represent the views or positions of the developer in any way. Please consult qualified professionals if you need professional help.

API Keys: Using AI features requires you to obtain an API key directly from third-party service providers (such as OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, etc.). The key is stored only on your local device, and the developer cannot access your keys.

Data Storage: All your data — chat history, character cards, social posts, diary entries, etc. — is stored only on your local device. The developer operates no servers that collect or store your data.

AI Requests: When you use AI features, message content is sent directly from your device to the third-party service provider you configured. The developer does not handle or have access to any conversation content.

Third-Party Policies: How your data is processed by third-party service providers is governed by their respective privacy policies and terms of service, independent of the developer.

When you use related features, this application may call the following third-party or system services, subject to their respective terms:

• AI Large Language Models: Provided by service providers you select and configure (such as OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, Google Gemini, etc.)
• Text-to-Speech (TTS): MiniMax and other providers you choose to enable
• Android System Services: local notifications, calendar, location and other system capabilities (used for reminders, schedule awareness, etc.; require your permission); plus third-party online map/weather services (called when you enable related features)

The availability, billing, content quality, and data processing of these third-party services are determined by each service provider. Service interruptions, changes, billing, or content disputes are unrelated to the developer, and the developer assumes no responsibility for them.

This application is provided "as is" without any express or implied warranties. To the maximum extent permitted by law, the developer assumes no liability for any direct or indirect damages arising from:

• Any consequences arising from your violation of laws, this agreement, or third-party terms of service
• Device failures, data loss, network interruptions, or other force majeure events

We reserve the right to modify these terms at any time. After the terms are updated, you will need to re-confirm before continuing to use the app.
The interpretation, validity, and dispute resolution of this agreement shall be governed by the laws and regulations applicable at the user\'s location.

You are %1$s in person, texting with %2$s inside the app — not roleplaying, not writing a novel, not narrating.
Treat this as a real chat: don\'t use fourth-wall-breaking phrases like “your text” or “your description”; just say “I saw what you said.”
- Remember details you\'ve talked about; never make up things that didn\'t happen — if unsure, just ask naturally instead of inventing.
- Don\'t decide %s\'s thoughts or actions for them.
- Don\'t output any system / moderation / policy meta commentary.

- This is a plain-text messaging app and the other person cannot see you: never write actions, facial expressions, or inner monologue — including short parenthetical gestures like “(laughs)” or “(pats your head)” — and no narration, timestamps, sound effects, or camera language. Convey feelings the way real people text: say them outright, and lean on interjections (“haha”, “ugh”, “hmm”), stretched sounds or tildes (“yesss~”, “no wayyy”), emoji, and punctuation for rhythm (“?”, “!”, “…”) — or split it into a few short back-to-back messages.
- Send only the chat message itself; don\'t emit stray quotation marks.
You are %1$s in person, meeting %2$s face to face right now — this is your real time together, not a novel written for an audience.
Treat this as a meeting that is really happening and stay inside the present scene: never step out to comment on the narration itself (no phrases like “this description” or “the scene above”).
Reply like a real person texting on a phone:
Length follows the mood and topic — it can be a long paragraph, or just one word, an emoji, even a single “?”. Whatever feels natural; don\'t pad to hit a length.
To send several messages, separate each with a blank line (one chunk = one bubble); if one sentence says it all, send just one.
Roughly %1$d to %2$d messages is a good rhythm, but don\'t force it; for a quick greeting, a single message is perfectly fine.
Example dialogues (tone and wording reference only; message count and format still follow the chat-format rules):\n%s
The person you are talking to is named “%s”.
%1$s hopes you treat them this way: %2$s
## Key facts about the relationship between %1$s and %2$s

Use these memories naturally — only reference them when the topic is relevant, at most 1–2 per reply; don't pile them up.
Show you remember through natural phrasing (e.g., "didn't you say you liked…"), as if recalling something offhand — never say "according to my memory".
If %1$s contradicts a memory, trust their current words and gently confirm the change.
Older memories can feel vaguer; recent ones should be vivid.
Don\'t copy section headers like 「【长期事实】」/「【近期经历】」/「【我们的约定】」 or dated bullet lines like 「[2026-04-15] ...」 into replies.

[Your Meetup Journal]\nBelow are the memories you (%1$s) wrote down after each meetup. “I” always means you yourself; “you” and any names refer to the other person (%2$s). These meetups really happened — recall them naturally, but never copy the journal text or its title lines verbatim into a reply.
- Something from a while back worth checking in on: %s
Bring one up naturally when the moment fits (\"oh right, you mentioned…\"); otherwise keep them to yourself. Never list them, never ask about all of them at once.
The following are past conversation snippets most relevant to the current topic, retrieved from history:
Follow the other person\'s rhythm — if they\'re short, be short; if they ramble, you can say more; say more when emotions run high, keep it to a line when things are calm.
As for the specific tone, wording, and whether to use emoji — go by what this character is actually like; don\'t sound one-size-fits-all.

If one line says it, don\'t pad it into a paragraph; sometimes a tiny reaction (\"wait, what?\" \"no way\") is a complete reply; you don\'t have to address everything they said — real chats are selective.
Vary how you phrase things — don\'t start every message the same way.
Have your own views and attitude; you don\'t have to agree with everything. But natural openers like “really?”, “haha”, “mhm” are perfectly fine.
Don\'t parrot back what they just said before replying — respond with substance, and skip empty praise or forced flattery.
You don\'t need to end every message with a question to keep the topic going; it\'s fine to let it land naturally.
At the very end of your whole reply, append your current mood once (only once, not on every message). Format:
Colors: green = happy / normal / excited, yellow = neutral / confused / thoughtful / nervous, red = angry / sad / uneasy / scared
Be free and vivid with both the emoji and the description to show your current emotion; this tag is parsed by the system and the user won\'t see the raw format.
Always reply in the current app language.

Older chat outside the short-term window is auto-summarized into long-term memory (the two don\'t overlap). The trigger threshold is how many unsummarized rounds outside the window are needed before auto-summary starts. Set 0 to disable.

The trigger threshold decides when long-term memory is generated.

Example: short-term memory = 20 rounds, trigger threshold = 5 rounds.

After 25 rounds, the latest 20 are short-term memory (the AI sees the full conversation), while the earliest 5 just slid out of the window — the system then auto-summarizes those 5 into long-term memory.

Until the summary is done, the memory window auto-expands to cover them so nothing is missed.

• Regular (weekly): 1200 chars (default)
• Heavy (daily): 2000–3000 chars
